question: Point out the INCORRECT response regarding infection by human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) and pregnancy:

options.opa: The scheduled cesarean does not reduce the vertical transmission rate of the virus.
options.opb: The pregnant woman will be offered the possibility of performing antiretroviral treatment whatever her stage of the disease, in order to prevent the vertical transmission of the virus.
options.opc: Vertical transmission of the virus is associated with maternal viral load.
options.opd: HIV serology must be offered to every pregnant woman at the first consultation, whatever the time of pregnancy.
options.ope: Women infected with HIV have an increased risk of spontaneous abortions, intrauterine fetal death and intrauterine growth retardation.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Scheduled cesarean" -> "does not reduce vertical transmission" -> "conflicts with evidence" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Antiretroviral treatment" -> "offered to pregnant women" -> "prevents vertical transmission" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Maternal viral load" -> "associated with vertical transmission" -> "consistent with evidence" -> 90%
CHAIN: "HIV serology" -> "offered at first consultation" -> "regardless of pregnancy stage" -> "standard practice" -> 90%
CHAIN: "HIV infection" -> "increased risk of spontaneous abortions" -> "increased risk of intrauterine fetal death" -> "increased risk of intrauterine growth retardation" -> 85%
analysis: The incorrect response is option 'opa'. Scheduled cesarean delivery can reduce the vertical transmission rate of HIV, especially when the maternal viral load is not optimally suppressed. This is a well-established practice to minimize the risk of mother-to-child transmission of HIV. The other options correctly describe aspects of HIV management in pregnancy, such as the importance of antiretroviral therapy, the association of transmission with maternal viral load, the recommendation for HIV testing, and the increased risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes in HIV-infected women.
